request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**How it works:** each of the four write endpoints has a new `audit` step, placed right after the change is saved and before the response is sent:
- `people.POST.yml` writes `PERSON_ADDED`
- `people/{personId}.PUT.yml` writes `PERSON_EDITED`
- `people/{personId}/claims.POST.yml` writes `CLAIM_ADDED`
- `claims/{claimId}.PUT.yml` writes `CLAIM_EDITED`

The steps are four new classes (`AuditPersonAdded`, `AuditPersonEdited`, `AuditClaimAdded`, `AuditClaimEdited`) that write through the existing `Audit` service. Lines are in the requested form, e.g. `CLAIM_EDITED sheet=<id> by=<user> person=Ada amount=6.00 date=2026-03-02`.

- **Amounts and dates** come from the same formatting the screen uses, so amounts always have two decimals and dates are `yyyy-mm-dd`.
- **Refused changes** never write a line. Every check (input rules, duplicate names, missing person or claim) runs before the save, so a refusal stops the request before the audit step. Any rule added later as an earlier step will work the same way.
- **Edits that change nothing** still write a line. The tests expect this: re-saving a grade of B as B, or an amount of 12.50 as 12.50, is recorded.
- **Claim edits** look up the claim's person to get the name, since the edit request doesn't carry it.

One limitation: the line is written inside the database transaction, before it commits. If the commit itself failed after that point, the file would hold a line for a change that wasn't stored. That shouldn't happen in normal use.

The front end needed no changes because it already sends the signed-in user with each change. I also added a one-line comment to each of the four endpoint YAML files saying what it records.
